brief.meaningEn: Very close to where someone lives or is based, without implying that a place is literally at the entrance.
brief.meaningZh: 離某人居住或所在之處很近，不必真的就在大門前。
brief.grammar: a place/activity is right on someone’s doorstep; the possessive identifies whose local area is meant.
brief.register: Common proximity idiom. Right emphasises closeness; an offer being nearby does not establish quality, opening hours or personal suitability.
brief.boundaryZh: 附近是位置，不保證免費、適合或隨時開放；也不是所有人的住處都近。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要交代對誰而言近，不能把一人附近的設施概括全城方便。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明住處附近的機會，保留需另查的安排。

listening.en: The rehearsal studio is right on our doorstep, so we can walk there after dinner; we still need to check whether a room is available on Thursday.
listening.zh: 排練室就在我們住處附近，晚飯後可走去；但仍需查星期四有沒有房。
listening.promptZh: 哪項已知，哪項仍待查？

options.en: The studio is close to home, but Thursday’s room availability is unconfirmed.
options.zh: 排練室近住處，但星期四有沒有房仍未確認。

options.en: A room has been reserved, although the journey from home remains unknown.
options.zh: 房間已預訂，但從住處去的路程仍未知。

options.en: The studio is close to the speaker’s workplace rather than home.
options.zh: 排練室近的是說話者工作地點，而非住處。

options.en: The speaker will attend a confirmed session immediately after dinner on Thursday.
options.zh: 說話者會在星期四晚飯後參加已確認的活動。

listening.explanationZh: doorstep交代近住處；仍要查有沒有房，不是已預訂或活動已定。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想先問這家排練室？
reply.promptEn: Why would you ask this rehearsal studio first?

options.en: It is right on our doorstep, so we could walk there after dinner.
options.zh: 它就在住處附近，晚飯後可走去。

options.en: We would not need a long journey from home to get there.
options.zh: 我們從家過去不用長途跋涉。

options.en: Being able to walk there would make an evening rehearsal easier to arrange.
options.zh: 能走去讓晚間排練較易安排。

options.en: It is close enough for us to check in person without a special trip across town.
options.zh: 它夠近，我們可親身查詢，不用特地跨區。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說近住處帶來的安排方便，未當作已訂到房。

scene.promptZh: 你搬家後發現社區史料室離家步行五分鐘，但它只在星期六開放；你想寫訊息提醒朋友先查時間。哪句準確？

options.en: The archive is right on my doorstep, though I need to plan around its Saturday opening.
options.zh: 史料室就在我住處附近，但我需按星期六開放安排。

options.en: The archive is far from my new home, so reaching it requires a trip across town.
options.zh: 史料室離新家很遠，要跨區才到。

options.en: The archive’s nearness means I can drop in after work on any weekday.
options.zh: 史料室近，所以我可任何平日下班後去。

scene.explanationZh: 五分鐘是近，但只周六開放，不能以距離推開放時間。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不是 right on your doorstep 這個位置說法所交代的事？

options.en: A facility is very near your home.
options.zh: 設施很近你的住處。

options.en: A nearby facility is necessarily well suited to the activity you want.
options.zh: 附近設施必然適合你想做的活動。

options.en: A local opportunity can be reached without travelling far from where you live.
options.zh: 本地機會不用離住處遠行便可接觸。

contrast.explanationZh: 位置近不等於用途、品質及安排都合適。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友因排練室近，想直接公布星期四地點，還未問有沒有房。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Check Thursday’s availability first, then tell the group if the nearby room can actually be used.
options.zh: 先查星期四有沒有房，確定附近房間可用才通知全組。

options.en: Ask everyone to walk over on Thursday and check availability once the group arrives.
options.zh: 請大家星期四走過去，到齊才查有沒有房。

options.en: Choose a studio across town without asking either place about Thursday.
options.zh: 不問兩處星期四情況，改選跨區排練室。

dialogue.explanationZh: 近可作優點，但宣布地點前仍需確認；不是先集合碰運氣或只因遠近反向選。

speaking.en: The small library is right on my doorstep, but I need to check when the reading group meets.
speaking.zh: 小圖書館就在住處附近，但我需查閱讀小組何時聚會。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說附近設施及待查安排。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編地方導覽，一位住戶說公園就在她家附近；草稿卻把這句擴成區內每個地址都一樣近。你只核過她家位置，想限定此句適用範圍，請其他地點另查，不把她的真實方便刪掉。用一至兩句英文寫給編輯。

examples.en: The park is right on her doorstep, but we have checked only that address, not every home in the district. Could we keep her local experience and avoid presenting it as a promise about the whole area?
examples.zh: 公園就在她家附近，但我們只核該地址，非全區每戶；可保她本地經驗，不寫成全區保證嗎？

examples.en: For this resident, the park is on her doorstep; that does not establish the distance from all the other streets. I would attribute the claim to her address and check the remaining locations separately.
examples.zh: 對此住戶，公園就在住處附近；這未確立其他每街距離，我會把說法限定她地址，其餘另查。

glossary.en: we have checked only that address

writing.selfCheckZh: 限定已核地址的地方導覽說法，保住戶實際方便，但不擴成所有街道同距離。

brief.meaningEn: Make an unusually great effort to help someone or accommodate a request.
brief.meaningZh: 為幫助某人或配合要求而付出很大、超乎一般的努力。
brief.grammar: bend/bent/bending over backwards to + verb; for + person. The phrase highlights effort, not a guaranteed successful outcome.
brief.register: Established effort idiom, often appreciative and sometimes critical when someone feels the effort is excessive.
brief.boundaryZh: 有很大努力不等於每項要求都已做到，也不表示對方必須接受無限額外工作。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可肯定已做的配合，同時承認時間或資源界限；拒一項要求不抹去先前努力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體安排說很大幫忙，而不把努力當結果或無限義務。

listening.en: The museum staff bent over backwards to include our late-arriving group: they moved the discussion and found a volunteer guide, though the conservation room still had to close at five.
listening.zh: 博物館職員為配合遲到的我們竭力幫忙，移了討論時間並找到義工導賞，但修護室仍需五點關閉。
listening.promptZh: 職員的努力及界限是甚麼？

options.en: They changed arrangements to help, but could not extend the conservation room’s opening.
options.zh: 他們改安排幫忙，但不能延長修護室開放。

options.en: They kept every arrangement unchanged and asked the whole group to leave immediately.
options.zh: 他們維持全部安排，請整組即時離開。

options.en: They extended the conservation room’s hours instead of finding a guide.
options.zh: 他們延長修護室時間，而不是找導賞。

options.en: They completed the conservation work themselves so the group could enter later.
options.zh: 他們親自完成修護工作，好讓小組稍後進去。

listening.explanationZh: 移討論及找導賞顯示努力，五點關閉仍是界限；沒有說修護工作已完成。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你特別感謝博物館職員？
reply.promptEn: Why are you especially grateful to the museum staff?

options.en: They bent over backwards to fit us in, moving the discussion and finding a guide.
options.zh: 他們移討論及找導賞，竭力把我們安排進去。

options.en: They changed more than one arrangement to help our delayed group.
options.zh: 他們為遲到的我們改了不只一項安排。

options.en: A volunteer guide was found even though we arrived later than planned.
options.zh: 雖然我們比原定遲到，仍找到義工導賞。

options.en: They made room for our discussion rather than simply cancelling it.
options.zh: 他們為討論騰出時間，沒有直接取消。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各有已做配合的具體理由，不把五點後開放當已實現。

scene.promptZh: 同事為讓你照顧家人，已換了兩次排練時間，也幫你整理缺席內容；但周五演出不能再改。你想感謝而不要求無限配合。哪句貼切？

options.en: You have bent over backwards to help me, and I understand that Friday’s performance has to stay as planned.
options.zh: 你已竭盡所能幫我，我理解星期五演出要照原定。

options.en: Keeping Friday unchanged shows that you made no effort to accommodate me earlier.
options.zh: 星期五不改，顯示你之前沒花心力配合我。

options.en: Since you changed rehearsal twice, the performance has already been moved as well.
options.zh: 既然你改過兩次排練，演出也已改期。

scene.explanationZh: 兩次改及整理內容是努力，演出不改不抹去它，也不代表演出已移。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最混淆 bend over backwards 的努力與結果？

options.en: Someone makes several substantial changes to help, but one request remains impossible.
options.zh: 有人作多項實質改動幫忙，但一項要求仍無法做到。

options.en: A person’s great effort means the requested outcome must already have been achieved.
options.zh: 某人很努力，表示所求結果必定已達成。

options.en: A speaker can appreciate extensive help while accepting a limit.
options.zh: 說話者可感謝大量幫助，同時接受界限。

contrast.explanationZh: 重點是大量努力，不是已達成每個結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 團員想因職員不能延長五點開放，就在致謝信刪去所有已提供的配合。哪個回應較公平？

options.en: Thank them for the changed discussion and guide, while noting that we still missed the conservation room.
options.zh: 感謝改討論和找導賞，同時說我們仍未看修護室。

options.en: Describe only the missed room and leave out the arrangements that helped us.
options.zh: 只寫沒看到修護室，略去有幫忙的安排。

options.en: Ask the volunteer to stay after closing instead of arranging an earlier visit another day.
options.zh: 不另日提早探訪，改請義工閉館後留下。

dialogue.explanationZh: 具體肯定與未做到可以同時記錄；不只刪正面或把幫助視為再延時義務。

speaking.en: She bent over backwards to make the rehearsal accessible, although one change still needed approval.
speaking.zh: 她竭力令排練方便參與，但一項改動仍待批准。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說具體努力及未定部分。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友幫你做雙語故事小冊，已逐頁試讀、整理陌生詞及錄了一段示範；你現在想謝他，並說剩下的封面文字會自己處理，不再把所有工作推給他。用一至兩句英文寫謝訊。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說已付出的具體努力，感謝後接回自己可做的工作；不把努力當他日後必須承包全部。

examples.en: You have bent over backwards to help with my booklet, reading every page and recording an example. Thank you; I will take care of the remaining cover text myself.
examples.zh: 你逐頁看又錄示範，竭力幫我的小冊；謝謝，剩下封面文字我會自己處理。

examples.en: Thank you for bending over backwards to make the story easier to follow, especially by explaining the unfamiliar words. You have done plenty, and I can finish the cover wording.
examples.zh: 謝謝你竭力讓故事更易理解，尤其解釋陌生詞；你已做很多，封面措辭我可完成。

takeaways.zh: 他們竭力幫新人適應，包括每次活動後回答問題。

titleEn: put time back in your hands

brief.meaningEn: Save someone time so that they have more control over how to use it.
brief.meaningZh: 替某人省下時間，使他能更自主安排用途。
brief.grammar: a change can/does put time back in someone’s hands; put/puts/putting. The time is saved or freed for choice, not literally handed over.
brief.register: Productive time-as-possession metaphor, not a separate fixed grammatical idiom. Explain the actual time saving rather than promise a universal effect.
brief.boundaryZh: 有省下的時間未等於休息或完成新工作，怎用仍需選擇；不能單憑換工具就假定更省時。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需有減少等待、路程或重做的具體根據，不把方便和空閒結果混為一談。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋省時來源及自主安排，不宣稱時間自動用好。

sources.sentence: A direct train can put time back in your hands.

listening.en: Combining the two collection trips put time back in my hands: instead of crossing town twice, I had an hour free, and I chose to spend it reading rather than add another errand.
listening.zh: 把兩次取件合併，讓我省下可自己安排的時間；不用兩次跨區，多了一小時，我選閱讀而不是再加差事。
listening.promptZh: 省時的來源與用途是甚麼？

options.en: One combined journey freed an hour, which the speaker chose to use for reading.
options.zh: 合併路程騰出一小時，說話者選用來閱讀。

options.en: The speaker made two trips more quickly and used the extra hour for another errand.
options.zh: 說話者較快做完兩次路程，再用多出一小時辦差事。

options.en: The combined journey had been arranged, but the speaker had not yet chosen how to use the free hour.
options.zh: 合併路程已安排，但說話者還未選怎用空出一小時。

options.en: The combined trip took an extra hour, leaving less choice about the afternoon.
options.zh: 合併路程多用一小時，下午更難自主安排。

listening.explanationZh: 少一次跨區騰出一小時，閱讀是已說出的選擇；不是兩次更快、再辦差事、用途未選或反而多花時間。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想把取件安排在同一趟？
reply.promptEn: Why would you arrange both collections in one trip?

options.en: It puts time back in my hands by removing a second journey across town.
options.zh: 它免去第二次跨區，省下可自主安排的時間。

options.en: One journey would leave more of the afternoon for something I choose.
options.zh: 一次路程讓下午更多時間可自己選用途。

options.en: I would avoid repeating the travel, rather than trying to rush both trips.
options.zh: 我可避免重複路程，而不是兩趟都趕。

options.en: The saved travel time could become a quiet reading hour.
options.zh: 省下路程時間可變成安靜閱讀一小時。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代省去重複路程的理由或可能用途，未當省時自動等於完成更多。

scene.promptZh: 小組把每週報告改成一頁共用摘要，不再讓每人重抄相同資料；省下的半小時由各人選擇閱讀或提早離開。哪句準確？

options.en: The shared summary puts time back in our hands by reducing repeated copying.
options.zh: 共用摘要減少重抄，讓我們省下時間自行安排。

options.en: The summary gives us more control because it adds another half-hour of copying.
options.zh: 摘要多加半小時重抄，所以讓我們更能自主安排。

options.en: Everyone has already used the saved half-hour to complete the same additional report.
options.zh: 每人已用省下半小時完成同一份額外報告。

scene.explanationZh: 減重複是來源，用途可選，不是額外重抄或已做相同新報告。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最缺乏 put time back in your hands 所說的省時與自主安排？

options.en: A simpler process removes repeated work and leaves time for a chosen activity.
options.zh: 較簡流程減重複工作，留下時間做自選活動。

options.en: A new system takes the same time and requires every remaining minute for another assigned task.
options.zh: 新系統用時相同，每個剩餘分鐘也需做另一指派任務。

options.en: A shorter journey gives someone an interval they can decide how to use.
options.zh: 較短路程給某人一段可自主安排的空檔。

contrast.explanationZh: 同樣用時及沒有可自行安排的空檔，未有這裏的省時益處。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想在合併取件省下的一小時立即加差事，說省時就代表每人應辦更多；你原想保留閱讀。哪個回應最好？

options.en: We saved the travel time, but I would like to choose how to use my hour rather than automatically add an errand.
options.zh: 我們省了路程，但我想自己選怎用這小時，不自動加差事。

options.en: Use the hour for another collection first, and decide whether there is reading time afterwards.
options.zh: 先用這小時再取一次件，之後再看有沒有閱讀時間。

options.en: Make the two separate journeys again so no one needs to discuss how to use the saving.
options.zh: 改回兩次獨立路程，便不用討論省下時間怎用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 省時與使用選擇分開，不是自動再填任務或取消省時來避談。

speaking.en: The simpler booking process puts time back in our hands, leaving us free to plan the activity itself.
speaking.zh: 較簡訂位流程省下可自主安排的時間，讓我們可規劃活動本身。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再解釋減少甚麼工作及有何選擇。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在家練樂器，已跟家人約好每次練完把樂譜放回同一小架，下次不用先找譜。你想在給自己的練習筆記說明這省時做法，並決定把空出十分鐘用來慢練難段，而不是增加整首重複次數。用一至兩句英文寫筆記。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明省去找譜及自己選慢練難段，不把空檔當必須重複整首或已練好難段。

examples.en: Keeping the music on the same shelf puts time back in my hands because I no longer search for it before practice. I will use the spare ten minutes to work slowly on the difficult passage.
examples.zh: 樂譜放同一架，不用練前找譜，省下可自主安排時間；我會用多出十分鐘慢練難段。

examples.en: Putting the sheets away together can put time back in my hands for the next session. Instead of playing the whole piece again, I want to spend the saved time on a few difficult bars.
examples.zh: 樂譜收在一起可替下次省下自主安排時間；我想用省下時間練幾個難小節，不是再彈整首。

takeaways.en: The shorter check-in puts time back in our hands, so we can choose a calmer start to the workshop.
takeaways.zh: 較短報到省下可自主安排的時間，讓我們選較從容開始工作坊。

takeaways.en: A clear shared list put time back in her hands by cutting the time she spent searching for updates.
takeaways.zh: 清楚共用清單減少找更新的時間，讓她省下時間自己安排。

brief.meaningEn: Consume a substantial block of time, such as half or all of a day, often leaving less time for other plans.
brief.meaningZh: 耗去大段時間，例如半天或整天，常使其他事情可用時間變少。
brief.grammar: A journey or task eats/ate/has eaten up half the day, the whole day, or an entire day. State actual hours when timing matters; the quantity depends on context.
brief.register: Common conversational eat up time metaphor; a colleague may use it to explain scheduling pressure. Half the day can be approximate, while the whole day describes all available daytime.
brief.boundaryZh: 耗時不表示事情沒價值或做錯，也不必整整十二小時；需要時間表時應給實際時段。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因花時間就斷言無用；可保留活動價值而調整其後計劃。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述大量時間消耗及其後安排，分清耗時與價值判斷。

listening.en: Sorting the mixed recordings ate up half the day, from nine until noon; we found useful interview clips, but had to move the editing session to tomorrow.
listening.zh: 整理混雜錄音耗去半天，九點至中午；我們找到有用訪談片段，但剪輯需移到明天。
listening.promptZh: 時間消耗帶來甚麼後果？

options.en: Sorting took the morning and yielded useful clips, while editing was postponed.
options.zh: 整理用了早上，也找到有用片段，剪輯則延期。

options.en: Editing was completed during the morning before any recordings were sorted.
options.zh: 未整理錄音前，早上已完成剪輯。

options.en: No useful clips were found, so all the recordings were discarded.
options.zh: 沒找到有用片段，所以錄音全丟棄。

options.en: The sorting took twelve hours, ending late at night.
options.zh: 整理用了十二小時，深夜才結束。

listening.explanationZh: 明說九至十二，找到有用片段但剪輯延明天；半天不是十二小時固定計算。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼剪輯要移到明天？
reply.promptEn: Why has editing been moved to tomorrow?

options.en: Sorting ate up half the day, so we ran out of the time set aside for editing.
options.zh: 整理耗去半天，原留剪輯時間不夠了。

options.en: The morning went on finding the clips we needed.
options.zh: 早上用了來找需用片段。

options.en: We spent nine until noon organising the mixed recordings.
options.zh: 九點至中午都在整理混雜錄音。

options.en: The useful sorting work took the interval we had expected to use for editing.
options.zh: 有用的整理工作占了原預期剪輯的時段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答時間安排原因，不把耗時說成沒價值或剪輯已完成。

scene.promptZh: 周末你試一道新食譜，從九點至中午才煮好，學到新技法；原定午前寫信只好改到午後。哪句準確？

options.en: Trying the recipe ate up half the day, but I learnt a technique and can write my letter later.
options.zh: 試食譜耗去半天，但我學到技法，稍後仍可寫信。

options.en: The letter was finished before noon because trying the recipe took very little time.
options.zh: 試食譜只用很短時間，所以信在中午前已寫好。

options.en: The time spent cooking shows that learning the technique had no value.
options.zh: 花時間煮食，顯示學那技法沒有價值。

scene.explanationZh: 用了早上令寫信需改期，但學到技法仍有價值，不是已寫好信。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不受 eat up half the day 支持？

options.en: A task has used a large portion of the available day.
options.zh: 任務用了當天可用時間的大部分。

options.en: The task was necessarily worthless because it took that long.
options.zh: 任務花了那麼久，所以必然毫無價值。

options.en: The speaker may need to revise the remaining schedule.
options.zh: 說話者或需重排餘下時間。

contrast.explanationZh: 耗時描述份量，不自動評價成果無用。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把早上整理稱「浪費半天」，但那些片段正好是剪輯所需；你想保留價值也承認進度。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Sorting the clips ate up half the day, but we found what we need; let us revise the editing plan rather than call the work wasted.
options.zh: 整理片段耗去半天，但我們找到了所需素材；應重排剪輯計劃，不把工作全稱浪費。

options.en: Keep the old editing deadline and skip checking whether the selected clips are usable.
options.zh: 保留舊剪輯限期，不再檢查所選片段可不可用。

options.en: Repeat the entire sorting tomorrow before deciding how much editing time remains.
options.zh: 明天再完整整理一次，才決定剪輯還有多少時間。

dialogue.explanationZh: 整理耗時，也找到所需素材；承認半天的時間代價，同時按現況重排剪輯，不必少核查或無理由重做。

speaking.en: The unexpected checks ate up half the day, so we moved the discussion to the afternoon.
speaking.zh: 意外多出的檢查耗去半天，所以討論移到下午。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說耗時對其後安排的影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你先前以為朋友遲交海報是沒花時間幫忙，現在才知她九點至中午都在陪新同學找回放錯的資料夾。你想撤回「甚麼也沒做」的話，承認她幫忙用了半天；交稿安排可另談，不把她的付出抹掉。用一至兩句英文寫道歉。

examples.en: Helping the new student find the folder ate up half the day, and I was wrong to say you had done nothing. I should have asked what happened before judging your effort; we can discuss the poster deadline separately.
examples.zh: 幫新同學找資料夾耗半天，我說你甚麼沒做是錯；評你付出前應先問發生甚麼，海報限期可另談。

examples.en: I now understand that finding the misplaced folder ate up half a day of your time. I am sorry I treated the late poster as proof that you had not helped anyone, rather than asking about the work I had not seen.
examples.zh: 我現在明白找放錯資料夾耗你半天；很抱歉把海報遲當你沒幫任何人，而非問自己未見的工作。

glossary.en: the work I had not seen

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫實際道歉，以得知的耗時幫忙修正原先評價；把付出及另需協商的交稿分開。

takeaways.en: Cataloguing the donated books ate up the whole day, so the team left the display layout until morning.
takeaways.zh: 替捐贈書籍編目耗去整天，團隊便把展示佈局留待翌日早上處理。

takeaways.en: The journey can eat up half the day, so I would leave the rest of the afternoon free.
takeaways.zh: 路程可耗去半天，所以我會讓下午其餘時間保持空檔。

brief.meaningEn: A place, activity or group that forms an especially active and important centre of a larger community or organisation.
brief.meaningZh: 在較大社群或組織中，特別活躍又重要的中心場所、活動或群體。
brief.grammar: X is/was the beating heart of + community/organisation/place; explain the ongoing activity and connections that make it central.
brief.register: Conventional heart metaphor with beating emphasising living activity. It expresses an interpretation of importance, not a measurable official rank.
brief.boundaryZh: 重要活躍核心不等於唯一有價值部分、地圖正中央或所有人每天都來；需有實際活動根據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以肯定連繫人及活動的作用，不因建築大、位置中央就套此比喻。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以日常參與及連繫說核心作用，保留其他地方貢獻。

listening.en: The repair café became the beating heart of our neighbourhood project: neighbours brought skills and questions there each week, while the library and youth club continued to run their own useful activities.
listening.zh: 維修聚會成了本區計劃充滿活力的核心；鄰居每周帶技能和問題來，圖書館及青年會也繼續有各自有用活動。
listening.promptZh: 維修聚會為甚麼被稱核心？

options.en: It regularly brought neighbours’ skills and questions together within a wider network.
options.zh: 它定期把鄰居技能和問題連起來，是較大網絡的一部分。

options.en: It took over the library’s and youth club’s activities after those places stopped operating.
options.zh: 圖書館和青年會停運後，它接管兩處活動。

options.en: It was selected because its building was the largest, rather than because of people’s participation.
options.zh: 它因建築最大而非人們參與被選中。

options.en: It mattered only during the opening ceremony and had no regular gatherings afterwards.
options.zh: 它只在開幕重要，之後沒有定期聚會。

listening.explanationZh: 每周交流顯示活力及連繫，其他活動仍有用；未說建築排名或只開幕。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你把維修聚會稱為社區計劃的核心？
reply.promptEn: Why do you call the repair café central to the neighbourhood project?

options.en: It is the beating heart of the project because neighbours regularly share skills and seek help there.
options.zh: 鄰居常在此分享技能求助，所以它是計劃充滿活力的核心。

options.en: It gives people a regular place to connect what they know with what others need.
options.zh: 它定期讓人把所知與別人需要連起來。

options.en: The weekly gatherings keep neighbours involved beyond a single event.
options.zh: 每周聚會讓鄰居不只在一次活動參與。

options.en: People bring both practical knowledge and questions, so the exchanges keep developing.
options.zh: 人們帶來實用知識和問題，交流因而持續發展。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用定期交流及參與答核心作用，而非只有地圖或建築。

scene.promptZh: 合唱團沒有固定排練室，但每周一起聽新旋律、提議分部的晚間聚會，令不同年齡團員持續合作；場地輪流借用。哪句貼切？

options.en: The weekly music-making is the beating heart of the choir, even though its meeting place changes.
options.zh: 每周一起做音樂是合唱團充滿活力的核心，即使聚會地點會變。

options.en: The changing venue means the choir has no regular activity that brings its members together.
options.zh: 場地會變，表示合唱團沒有連結成員的定期活動。

options.en: The most central venue on the map must be the heart of the choir, regardless of what happens there.
options.zh: 無論有甚麼活動，地圖最中央場地必是合唱團核心。

scene.explanationZh: 核心可是一項持續共同活動，不必固定建築或地圖中點。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個根據最不足以支持 the beating heart of 這個比喻？

options.en: A group hosts regular exchanges that sustain a wider community’s participation.
options.zh: 群體定期交流，維持較大社群的參與。

options.en: A building is at the geographical centre, but nothing there currently connects people or activities.
options.zh: 建築在地理中央，但目前沒有連繫人或活動的作用。

options.en: An activity repeatedly brings members’ ideas into shared work.
options.zh: 活動持續把成員想法帶入共同工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 地理中央本身未顯示活躍而重要的連繫作用。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴要把社區計劃介紹只寫維修聚會，刪去仍有活動的圖書館及青年會，理由是「核心應包含一切」。哪個回應較準確？

options.en: Explain how the café connects neighbours, while keeping the library and youth club’s distinct contributions in the account.
options.zh: 說明聚會怎連繫鄰居，也保留圖書館和青年會各自貢獻。

options.en: Move the other activities into the café’s description without saying which group actually runs them.
options.zh: 把其他活動放進聚會介紹，不說真正由哪個團體舉辦。

options.en: Replace the café’s weekly exchanges with building-size comparisons when explaining its importance.
options.zh: 解釋重要時，用建築大小比較取代每周交流。

dialogue.explanationZh: 重要核心不等於包辦，應有活動根據並保留別人貢獻。

speaking.en: The shared kitchen is the beating heart of the centre, where neighbours meet and exchange ideas each week.
speaking.zh: 共用廚房是中心充滿活力的核心，鄰居每周在此聚會交流想法。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用持續活動說明核心作用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編社團十年回顧，舊紀錄顯每周交換故事原是最活躍核心，後來停了三年；今年有新人重新組織，已聚兩次。你想寫出核心角色的失落與可能恢復，不把新兩次當已重回從前，也不一直用現在式說從未停過。用一至兩句英文寫回顧。

examples.en: The weekly story exchange was once the beating heart of the club, before its three-year pause left that connection missing. Two new meetings suggest a possible return, but we are still learning whether the activity can regain its former role.
examples.zh: 每周故事交流曾是社團活力核心，停三年後那連繫缺了；兩次新聚會顯或可回來，但能否恢復原角色仍待了解。

examples.en: What had been the beating heart of the club fell silent for three years, and newcomers have now begun the exchange again. These first meetings mark an early renewal; they do not yet show that the old pattern has been restored.
examples.zh: 曾是社團活力核心的活動沉寂三年，新人現開始重辦交流；這些首場聚會標初步復甦，還未顯舊模式已恢復。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫有時間變化的回顧，分曾是核心、停辦及初步復甦，保新人努力而不以兩次證已重建持續參與。

takeaways.en: The evening sessions became the beating heart of the arts project, keeping people involved between performances.
takeaways.zh: 晚間活動成了藝術計劃活力核心，讓人們在演出之間持續參與。

takeaways.en: For many members, the small workshop is the beating heart of the club because it is where ideas turn into shared projects.
takeaways.zh: 對很多成員，小工場是學會活力核心，想法在此化為共同計劃。

brief.meaningEn: A stage at which someone must consider an important choice between possible directions.
brief.meaningZh: 需要考慮在不同方向之間作重要選擇的階段。
brief.grammar: be/find oneself at a crossroads; a crossroads keeps the final s even when referring to one decision point. The choice may concern study, work or a shared project.
brief.register: Established decision metaphor. Unlike the crossroads of two subjects, this use focuses on a decision about the next direction, not an intersection of disciplines.
brief.boundaryZh: 面臨抉擇不表示已選好、只有兩條路或選錯便不能調整；需交代實際選項及待了解資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 重要關口可以先查詢、試一小步或延後決定，不必以焦慮代替比較。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出抉擇及未定部分，提出可幫比較的下一步。

listening.en: Our reading group was at a crossroads: we could keep the monthly meetings or begin a small publishing project, but we had not chosen either; first we asked how much time members could offer.
listening.zh: 閱讀小組面臨重要抉擇：可維持每月聚會，或開始小型出版計劃，但兩者都未選；我們先問成員可投入多少時間。
listening.promptZh: 關口在哪裏，決定到甚麼階段？

options.en: The group was comparing future directions and gathering time commitments before choosing.
options.zh: 小組比較未來方向，在選擇前收集可投入時間。

options.en: The publishing project had already replaced every monthly meeting.
options.zh: 出版計劃已取代每次月聚會。

options.en: The members had confirmed that both plans required exactly the same time.
options.zh: 成員已確認兩計劃需時完全相同。

options.en: The group had ruled out publishing and was asking only which date to use for the next monthly meeting.
options.zh: 小組已排除出版，只問下一次月聚用哪天。

listening.explanationZh: 兩個方向都未選，先查可投入時間；不是已出版、兩案同時長或已排除出版只定日期。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你們先問成員可投入多少時間？
reply.promptEn: Why are you asking how much time members can offer before making the decision?

options.en: We are at a crossroads, and knowing people’s availability will help us compare the two directions.
options.zh: 我們面臨抉擇，知道大家可投入時間有助比較兩方向。

options.en: The choice between meetings and publishing depends partly on what members can sustain.
options.zh: 聚會與出版之間的選擇，部分取決成員可持續做到甚麼。

options.en: We do not want to commit to a project before understanding the work people can offer.
options.zh: 未了解大家可提供工作前，我們不想先答應計劃。

options.en: The information will help us judge whether publishing fits alongside people’s other commitments.
options.zh: 資料可幫判斷出版是否配合大家其他責任。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答先查時間對方向選擇的作用，並非已決定後才問。

scene.promptZh: 你完成一年陶藝入門課，正比較繼續練基本功或參加展覽班，想先看課程要求，再決定；尚未報名。哪句貼切？

options.en: I am at a crossroads and want to understand both courses before choosing my next step.
options.zh: 我面臨抉擇，想先了解兩課再選下一步。

options.en: I have already enrolled in the exhibition class and finished comparing the options.
options.zh: 我已報展覽班，也已完成比較。

options.en: Both courses have already been confirmed as requiring the same commitment, so no comparison remains.
options.zh: 兩課已確認需同樣投入，所以再沒比較待做。

scene.explanationZh: 下一步未定，課程要求也未比完；不是已報或已核同樣投入。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不是 at a crossroads 的抉擇用法？

options.en: A person is considering an important next direction.
options.zh: 某人考慮重要的下一步方向。

options.en: Two paths physically cross, with no decision about future plans being discussed.
options.zh: 兩路實際相交，沒有討論未來計劃的決定。

options.en: A group is comparing what it could become before making a commitment.
options.zh: 群體作承諾前，比較可朝甚麼方向發展。

contrast.explanationZh: 實際路口可用crossroads，但不是本課重要方向選擇的比喻。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把小組「面臨抉擇」寫成已選出版，還要發邀稿；其實大家尚在問可投入時間。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Say we are at a crossroads and are checking availability before deciding whether to invite submissions.
options.zh: 說我們面臨抉擇，正查可投入時間，之後才決定邀不邀稿。

options.en: Send the invitation now and compare the workload only after contributors have begun.
options.zh: 現在發邀稿，等投稿者開始才比較工作量。

options.en: Leave the availability question aside and choose the idea with the more attractive title.
options.zh: 不談可投入時間，選名稱較吸引的構思。

dialogue.explanationZh: 未選便保留未定及先查時間，不先帶動工作或用名稱替代安排比較。

speaking.en: We are at a crossroads, so I want to compare what each option would require before choosing a direction.
speaking.zh: 我們面臨抉擇，所以我想先比較每個選項要求，再選方向。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述重要選擇及比較需要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你續寫一個角色，她一直代全家安排事情，現收到主持社區故事活動的邀請，想嘗試又不願直接丟下家中責任。你想在獨白寫這個方向選擇，讓她先問家人可否分工，再決定是否接受，不把邀請當已接下。用一至兩句英文寫獨白。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把新角色與家事責任的方向選擇寫清楚，先談分工再答邀請，不假裝已接下或家人已同意。

examples.en: I am at a crossroads: I want to try hosting the storytelling event, but I need to discuss sharing the family tasks first. The invitation is a possibility, not a commitment I have already made.
examples.zh: 我面臨抉擇：想試主持故事活動，但需先談分擔家事；邀請是可能，不是我已作的承諾。

examples.en: Finding myself at a crossroads, I will ask my family what we can share before I answer the organiser. I want the new role to be a considered choice rather than another task I accept without discussion.

brief.meaningEn: Seem tiring and repetitive, often with little immediate enjoyment.
brief.meaningZh: 感覺疲累、反覆，往往缺少即時樂趣。
brief.grammar: a routine/task begins to feel like a grind; feels/felt/feeling. This productive feel-like frame evaluates how a particular activity is experienced; the daily grind names a demanding everyday routine.
brief.register: Conventional grind-as-demanding-work noun image in a feeling comparison. A task can have value while still feeling laborious to a participant.
brief.boundaryZh: 感到乏味不等於活動沒有價值、能力不足或人人同感；可說哪個部分重複及怎調整。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需區分本人感受與成果，不能只因厭倦就聲稱任務不需要做。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明重複工作的主觀負擔，提出不忽略目的的改動。

listening.en: Copying the same rehearsal notes into three separate files began to feel like a grind; the notes were useful, but I wanted one shared version so we could spend more time trying the changes.
listening.zh: 把同一排練筆記抄進三個獨立檔案，開始讓我感到乏味費力；筆記有用，但我想用一份共用版，多些時間試改動。
listening.promptZh: 不滿的是甚麼，仍肯定甚麼？

options.en: Repeated copying felt laborious, while the notes themselves remained useful.
options.zh: 重複抄寫感覺費力，但筆記本身仍有用。

options.en: Trying changes during rehearsal was the unwanted repetition, so the speaker wanted only copying.
options.zh: 排練試改動才是不想要的重複，所以說話者只想抄寫。

options.en: The speaker had already replaced the files and stopped recording any notes.
options.zh: 說話者已換檔案，也停止所有記錄。

options.en: The notes contained no useful information, and their accuracy was the stated problem.
options.zh: 筆記沒有有用資料，所述問題是內容準確性。

listening.explanationZh: 重複抄三份是負擔來源，想改流程而非停記或否定內容。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想改用一份共用排練筆記？
reply.promptEn: Why would you prefer one shared set of rehearsal notes?

options.en: Copying the same material feels like a grind, and one version would leave more time to try the changes.
options.zh: 抄同樣資料令人乏味費力，一份版可多留時間試改動。

options.en: We could keep the useful notes without repeating the copying three times.
options.zh: 我們可保留有用筆記，不重複抄三次。

options.en: The repeated file work is tiring me before we get to the practical rehearsal.
options.zh: 未到實際排練，重複檔案工作已讓我疲累。

options.en: A shared version would reduce the routine work while preserving the information we need.
options.zh: 共用版可減例行工作，同時保留所需資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以重複抄寫負擔答原因，未把筆記用途抹去。

scene.promptZh: 你每天臨摹同一組字，知道可練筆畫，但近日沒機會把它用在自己的短句，覺得像做完又重做；你仍想練好。哪句準確？

options.en: The repeated copying feels like a grind to me, though I still want to improve and try using the strokes in a short sentence.
options.zh: 反覆臨摹讓我感到乏味費力，但仍想進步，試把筆畫用在短句。

options.en: The copying has become effortless and enjoyable, and I want no change in the practice.
options.zh: 臨摹已變毫不費力又愉快，我完全不想改練習。

options.en: Feeling tired establishes that practising the strokes has no purpose.
options.zh: 感到疲累確立了練筆畫沒有目的。

scene.explanationZh: 可承認重複負擔，仍保留進步目的與應用嘗試，不把疲累等同無用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最超出 feels like a grind 的感受？

options.en: The activity feels laborious and repetitive to the person.
options.zh: 活動對那人感覺費力且反覆。

options.en: The task cannot have any value because the person finds it tiresome.
options.zh: 那人覺乏味，表示任務不可能有價值。

options.en: The speaker may want a different way to carry out the same useful purpose.
options.zh: 說話者或想換做法達成同一有用目的。

contrast.explanationZh: 主觀負擔不取消任務目的或價值。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴聽你說抄筆記乏味，便提議連記錄都取消；你其實想減重複保留內容。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The repeated copying feels like a grind, not the idea of keeping notes; let us use one shared record.
options.zh: 乏味費力的是重抄，不是記筆記本身；用一份共用記錄吧。

options.en: Stop recording the changes and rely only on what each person happens to remember.
options.zh: 停止記改動，只靠各人碰巧記得甚麼。

options.en: Keep all three copies and add a fourth summary before we test whether one version would work.
options.zh: 未試一份版可不可用，先保三份再加第四份摘要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 減重複與保資訊可同時做，不是取消目的或未試就加重流程。

speaking.en: The routine began to feel like a grind, so I asked whether we could keep its useful purpose with less repeated work.
speaking.zh: 例行工作開始讓我感到乏味費力，所以我問可否少些重複仍保有用目的。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分感受、用途及可改做法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你答應本周協助核舊訪問逐字稿，工作重複費力，但要讓受訪者的話準確留下，你願完成自己承諾的一份。你想向伙伴誠實說感受，同時清楚這次能負責的範圍，不提另一套效率方案，也不假裝自己很享受。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: Checking the transcript feels like a grind, but I want the speaker’s words to be kept accurately. I will finish the section I promised this week, while being clear that I cannot take on the whole archive.
examples.zh: 核逐字稿讓我覺乏味費力，但想說話者字句準確保留；本周我會完成答應部分，也說清不能接整個檔案。

examples.en: This work has begun to feel like a grind to me, even though I value why we are doing it. I am choosing to complete my agreed section, not claiming that I enjoy every minute or can commit to all the remaining material.
examples.zh: 我雖重視目的，這工作已開始乏味費力；我選完成議定部分，不是假裝每刻享受或可接全部餘料。

writing.selfCheckZh: 誠實表達主觀費力與仍重視目的，承擔自己有界定的承諾，不假裝每刻享受，也不把負擔說成全工作無價值。

takeaways.en: The long checklist felt like a grind after several identical sessions, although it still helped us catch missed steps.
takeaways.zh: 多次相同活動後，長清單令人乏味費力，但仍幫我們找漏步。

takeaways.en: When practice starts feeling like a grind, I ask which repetition is useful and where a new application could help.
takeaways.zh: 練習開始讓我感到乏味費力時，我會問哪些重複有用，以及哪裏可試新應用。

brief.meaningEn: Continuously or repeatedly every day over a period, emphasising regular persistence.
brief.meaningZh: 在一段時間內每天持續或反覆進行，強調經常性與持續。
brief.grammar: do something day in, day out; often separated by a comma. Context gives the period and whether the repetition is valued or tiring.
brief.register: Established rhythmic time phrase. It may praise persistence or express monotony; it does not by itself say that the task is enjoyable, useless or done every hour.
brief.boundaryZh: 每天持續不等於全天無休，也不自動帶正負評價；若是安排他人工作，仍需說明輪值而非要求一人永不休息。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可形容一項團隊服務每天持續，即使不同人輪流做。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述日常持續及具體時段，區分頻率、個人負擔與態度。

listening.en: For six weeks, volunteers checked the seedlings day in, day out, taking turns on a rota; each visit took a few minutes, and the daily notes helped them notice when a tray needed moving.
listening.zh: 六周來義工日復一日查看幼苗，按表輪流；每次只幾分鐘，每日筆記幫他們留意哪盤需移位。
listening.promptZh: 持續的安排是怎樣？

options.en: Checks happened each day, with different volunteers sharing short visits.
options.zh: 每天都有查看，不同義工分擔短探訪。

options.en: One volunteer stayed beside the seedlings every hour for six weeks.
options.zh: 一位義工六周每小時都守在幼苗旁。

options.en: The group inspected the seedlings only once at the end of the six weeks.
options.zh: 小組只在六周結束時查看一次幼苗。

options.en: The volunteers stopped keeping notes because the daily visits provided no useful information.
options.zh: 每日探訪沒有有用資料，所以義工停止記筆記。

listening.explanationZh: 每天持續由輪值完成，每次幾分鐘，未等於一人全天守着或六周只一次。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你們保留每日輪值查看？
reply.promptEn: Why are you keeping the daily checking rota?

options.en: Checking day in, day out helped us notice when the seedlings needed a different position.
options.zh: 日復一日查看，幫我們留意幼苗何時需換位置。

options.en: Short regular visits made changes easier to notice across the six weeks.
options.zh: 六周內定期短探訪讓變化較易被留意。

options.en: The daily notes let the next volunteer compare the tray with how it had looked before.
options.zh: 每日筆記讓下一位義工比較苗盤與之前的情況。

options.en: Taking turns kept the observations going without one person doing every visit.
options.zh: 輪流讓觀察持續，不用一人做每次探訪。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各答每日觀察的作用或輪值支持，不把每天等同全天或一人。

scene.promptZh: 小說角色每天下班後花十五分鐘練發音，持續一個月，星期日也有短練；她覺得有進步，不是在抱怨無聊。哪句貼切？

options.en: She practised day in, day out for a month, fitting a short session around her working day.
options.zh: 她一個月日復一日練，配合下班時間安排短練。

options.en: The phrase means she disliked the practice, despite her stated satisfaction with progress.
options.zh: 詞組表示她不喜歡練習，儘管她說滿意進步。

options.en: She practised for the whole day and gave up going to work during that month.
options.zh: 她全日練習，該月不再上班。

scene.explanationZh: 每天短練與滿意進步可並存，詞組本身不等於討厭或全天。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能單憑 day in, day out 推出？

options.en: The activity happens repeatedly each day over the stated period.
options.zh: 活動在所述期間每天反覆發生。

options.en: The same person does it continuously without sleep or breaks.
options.zh: 同一人不睡不休持續做。

options.en: The context may present the repetition as persistence or monotony.
options.zh: 情境可把重複呈現為堅持或單調。

contrast.explanationZh: 頻率每天不等於同一人全天無休；態度要看上下文。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴寫花園回顧時想說每位義工六周每天都來，因服務「日復一日」；你們其實按表輪值。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Say the checks continued day in, day out, with volunteers taking different turns on the rota.
options.zh: 說查看日復一日持續，由義工按表分別輪值。

options.en: The rota means each volunteer checked only one day in the entire six weeks, with no repeat turns.
options.zh: 輪值表表示每位義工六周內只查看一天，沒有再輪到。

options.en: Describe the checks as one long visit rather than a series of short daily observations.
options.zh: 把查看寫成一次長探訪，不是一連串每日短觀察。

dialogue.explanationZh: 日復一日指每日服務持續，輪值未證人人每天到或每人只到一次；不是一次長探訪。

speaking.en: They kept the service running day in, day out by sharing the work across a clear rota.
speaking.zh: 他們用清楚輪值表分擔工作，讓服務日復一日持續。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分持續服務與個別輪值。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為家人的紀念冊寫一段謝語。祖父多年每天在早餐聽你講一小段故事，從不催你快說；你想肯定這種安靜持續的陪伴，不把它寫成他全天只照顧你。用一至兩句英文寫回憶。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用每天早餐短聆聽表達持續關注的價值，不把日復一日誇成祖父全天只陪伴自己。

examples.en: Day in, day out, you listened to my little stories at breakfast without rushing me. Those few quiet minutes made me feel that what I had to say mattered.
examples.zh: 日復一日，你早餐時聽我的小故事，不催我；那幾分鐘安靜陪伴讓我覺得自己說的事重要。

examples.en: You made time for my breakfast stories day in, day out, even when the rest of the day was busy. I remember the regular attention, not a grand gesture made only once.
examples.zh: 即使餘下日子忙，你仍日復一日留時間聽早餐故事；我記得的是持續關注，不是只一次大舉動。

takeaways.en: The team answered questions day in, day out, with a different volunteer covering each morning.
takeaways.zh: 團隊日復一日答問題，每朝由不同義工當值。

takeaways.en: She worked on a paragraph day in, day out until the narrator’s voice began to feel natural to her.
takeaways.zh: 她日復一日修改一段文字，直到敘述者聲音讓她感覺自然。

brief.meaningEn: A situation in which intense pressure or tension builds among the people involved.
brief.meaningZh: 身處其中的人承受強烈壓力或緊張不斷累積的情況。
brief.grammar: a room/workplace/event feels like/becomes a pressure cooker; explain the deadlines, demands or interpersonal tensions creating the pressure.
brief.register: Established pressure-vessel metaphor. It describes felt conditions rather than diagnosing a person or claiming that conflict is inevitable.
brief.boundaryZh: 壓力強不等於必有人爆發、所有人同感或一定已失敗；也不能只因人多便推很緊張。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需要具體要求及互動根據，改善可包括釐清優先次序、減同時要求或給回應空間。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述壓力來源，提出合情境的緩和安排，不只用強烈比喻代分析。

listening.en: The final rehearsal felt like a pressure cooker: three people were giving the actors different changes at once, and the director asked everyone to pause so one person could explain the priorities.
listening.zh: 最後排練像壓力不斷累積的環境：三人同時給演員不同改動，導演請大家停一停，讓一人解釋優先次序。
listening.promptZh: 壓力從哪裏來，怎先處理？

options.en: Simultaneous conflicting changes created pressure, so the director paused to clarify priorities through one speaker.
options.zh: 同時不同改動造成壓力，所以導演暫停，由一人釐清優先次序。

options.en: The actors had completed every change, and the director cancelled the performance.
options.zh: 演員已完成每項改動，導演取消演出。

options.en: The director asked three more people to give changes at the same time.
options.zh: 導演請多三人同時提改動。

options.en: The room was quiet because no changes had been requested during rehearsal.
options.zh: 沒人在排練提出改動，所以房間安靜。

listening.explanationZh: 多路同時改動是具體來源，停下及一人說明是先處理，不是已改完或加更多人。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼導演要先停一停，讓一個人說？
reply.promptEn: Why did the director pause the rehearsal and ask for one speaker?

options.en: The rehearsal had become a pressure cooker because actors were receiving different changes at once.
options.zh: 演員同時收到不同改動，排練變壓力累積環境。

options.en: The actors needed to know which change mattered first instead of following several voices together.
options.zh: 演員需知道先改甚麼，不是同時跟幾把聲。

options.en: Pausing could reduce the competing instructions long enough to agree on priorities.
options.zh: 暫停可減互相競爭指示，讓大家有時間議優先次序。

options.en: One clear explanation would address the confusion that was adding to the tension.
options.zh: 一個清楚解釋可處理令緊張增加的混亂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各答同時要求造成的問題與釐清需要，不把暫停等同放棄。

scene.promptZh: 一場小型改稿會只有四人，但每人被催即時回應三份互相矛盾意見，還未說完便被打斷，氣氛愈來愈繃緊。哪句準確？

options.en: The discussion has become a pressure cooker despite the small group, because demands are piling up without space to respond.
options.zh: 雖然人少，要求不斷加而無空間回應，討論已像壓力累積環境。

options.en: The meeting’s small size means the repeated interruptions are evidence of a relaxed exchange.
options.zh: 會議人少，所以反覆打斷是輕鬆交流的證據。

options.en: The group has already resolved the conflicting comments and ended the discussion calmly.
options.zh: 小組已解決矛盾意見，平靜結束討論。

scene.explanationZh: 人數少不抹去同時要求及被打斷的壓力，亦未說已解決。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由 a pressure cooker 的情境比喻推出？

options.en: People are facing intense demands or tension.
options.zh: 人們面對強烈要求或緊張。

options.en: A particular person will certainly lose control and cause conflict.
options.zh: 某人一定會失控造成衝突。

options.en: The account should identify what is creating the pressure.
options.zh: 敘述應指出甚麼正在造成壓力。

contrast.explanationZh: 比喻描述環境，並不預知某人必定失控。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說暫停排練便是承認演員不行，想繼續把所有改動一次喊出；你看到壓力來自指示衝突。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The pressure comes from competing changes; a short pause to agree on priorities can help the actors respond.
options.zh: 壓力來自改動衝突；短暫停下議優先次序，可幫演員回應。

options.en: Keep the instructions simultaneous and ask each actor to choose privately which voice to follow.
options.zh: 維持同時指示，讓每個演員私自選跟哪把聲。

options.en: Stop all future feedback rather than decide how to give the next change clearly.
options.zh: 不議下項改動怎講清楚，直接停以後所有回饋。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需改的是競爭指示流程，不是怪能力、任各人選或完全取消回饋。

speaking.en: The room felt like a pressure cooker until we separated the urgent questions from those that could wait.
speaking.zh: 我們把急問題與可等的分開之前，房間一直像壓力累積環境。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出壓力來源及具體釐清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你小說中兩兄妹在出發前收拾祖屋，一邊有搬運限時，一邊不斷翻出有感情的物件，互相催又說不出捨不得。你想寫一段旁白，用這比喻顯示多重壓力，再讓他們先留一箱未決物品，約之後慢談，不把關係寫成已破裂。用一至兩句英文寫。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以限時與感情拉扯說壓力，安排一箱稍後談，讓人物有空間而不是宣告必吵架或關係破裂。

examples.en: The old house felt like a pressure cooker as the moving deadline collided with things neither of them was ready to let go of. They set one box aside for later discussion instead of forcing every decision before departure.
examples.zh: 搬運限時遇上兩人未準備放下的物件，祖屋像壓力累積環境；他們先留一箱之後談，不強迫出發前決定全部。

examples.en: Packing had turned the house into a pressure cooker, with the clock pushing them faster than their feelings could follow. Keeping a box for undecided items gave them room to leave on time and return to the memories together.
examples.zh: 時鐘催得比情緒跟得快，收拾讓屋像壓力累積環境；留一箱未決物品，讓他們可準時走，之後一起重談記憶。

takeaways.en: The planning meeting became a pressure cooker when every request was treated as equally urgent.

brief.meaningEn: A very large or apparently extensive crowd, described through the image of a sea.
brief.meaningZh: 用海的意象形容很大或看起來延伸很廣的人群。
brief.grammar: see/face/walk into a sea of people; the phrase conveys visual scale, not an exact count or the crowd’s purpose.
brief.register: Conventional crowd metaphor. A viewpoint may reveal only part of a gathering; do not infer how everyone feels or why they came.
brief.boundaryZh: 視覺人多不等於已核人數、全體支持或失去秩序；要分所見與後續查問。
brief.misconceptionZh: 人群可以有秩序，亦可只是等車，不能單憑規模推活動成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能生動描述人群，同時保留位置、範圍及未知原因。

listening.en: From the gallery steps, I saw a sea of people in the square, with separate queues marked by signs; I could not tell which visitors had come for the exhibition and which were waiting for the evening buses.
listening.zh: 在畫廊梯級上，我見廣場一大片人群，有標示劃出不同隊伍；我不能分哪些來看展，哪些等晚班巴士。
listening.promptZh: 看得到甚麼，仍不知道甚麼？

options.en: A large crowd and marked queues were visible, but people’s reasons for being there were unclear.
options.zh: 看得到大片人群及有標示隊伍，但不清楚各人為何在那裏。

options.en: All the people had confirmed that they came only to see the exhibition.
options.zh: 所有人已確認只為看展而來。

options.en: The square was empty, and only the gallery staff were on the steps.
options.zh: 廣場空無一人，只有職員在梯級。

options.en: The observer had counted the exhibition visitors after checking each person’s destination.
options.zh: 觀察者查過每人目的地，已數好看展人數。

listening.explanationZh: 人群大與有隊可見，目的未分，不是展覽已核人數。

reply.promptZh: 你在畫廊外看見怎樣的景象？
reply.promptEn: What did you see outside the gallery?

options.en: A sea of people filled the square, with signs marking separate queues.
options.zh: 廣場是一大片人群，標示劃出不同隊。

options.en: There was a large crowd spread across the square.
options.zh: 大片人群分布廣場。

options.en: I could see different queues, but not tell everyone’s destination.
options.zh: 我可見不同隊伍，卻不能分每人的目的地。

options.en: The square looked full from the steps where I was standing.
options.zh: 從我站的梯級看，廣場像擠滿了人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答所見景象，未把每人目的或精確人數當已知。

scene.promptZh: 你從舞台側邊看見大批觀眾安靜站在繩線後，工作人員逐排引導；你想形容人多，不把它說成混亂。哪句貼切？

options.en: I faced a sea of people waiting behind the marked line while staff guided each row.
options.zh: 我面對一大片人群，在標線後等職員逐排引導。

options.en: The crowd’s size shows that nobody was following any queue or instruction.
options.zh: 人群規模顯示沒有人跟隊伍或指示。

options.en: The staff had finished guiding the last row, leaving the viewing area empty.
options.zh: 職員已引導完最後一排，觀看區空了。

scene.explanationZh: 規模大仍可有秩序；所述逐排引導還在進行，不是全散。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最超出 a sea of people 的描述？

options.en: A crowd appears very large from the described viewpoint.
options.zh: 從所述角度看，人群顯得很大。

options.en: Every person is there to support the same cause.
options.zh: 每人都為支持同一目的而來。

options.en: The writer can add where the crowd was seen.
options.zh: 作者可補在哪看到人群。

contrast.explanationZh: 視覺規模不證共同目的，需另有資訊。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把廣場人多直接算作展覽入場人數，但你看到其中也可能有等巴士的人。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Describe the sea of people we saw, then use checked admission figures for exhibition attendance.
options.zh: 描述所見人群，再用核過入場數字說看展人數。

options.en: Count everyone visible in the square as an exhibition visitor without distinguishing the queues.
options.zh: 不分隊伍，把廣場所見每人都算看展訪客。

options.en: Use only the nearest queue as the exhibition total, without checking where those people intend to go.
options.zh: 不問那些人想去哪，只用最近隊伍作看展總數。

dialogue.explanationZh: 所見人群與特定活動入場統計分開，不能任挑一隊或全算同目的。

speaking.en: I could see a sea of people beyond the entrance, but I did not know how many had come for our event.
speaking.zh: 入口外我可見一大片人群，但不知多少為我們活動而來。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分所見規模及未核人數。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫舞台劇中的人物視角。第一次上台的角色只看見一大片觀眾，找不到答應來的姐姐；你想保留她緊張卻仍開始說首句，而不寫「人人都在笑她」這種她不知道的內心。用一至兩句英文寫片段。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用人物所見的人群及找不到姐姐寫緊張，接開始說話的動作，不把未知觀眾心意當事實。

examples.en: She faced a sea of people and could not pick out her sister, though she knew someone familiar might be there. She held the first line in her mind and began before she could guess what the audience thought.
examples.zh: 她面對一大片人群，找不到姐姐，雖知道熟人或在場；她記着首句，在猜觀眾想法之前開始說。

examples.en: Beyond the lights was a sea of people, not a set of faces she could read. Unable to find her sister, she took a breath and spoke the opening words anyway.
examples.zh: 燈光外是一大片人群，不是她看得懂的幾張臉；找不到姐姐，她仍吸口氣，說出開場。

takeaways.en: The balcony gave us a view of a sea of people moving slowly towards the station exits.
takeaways.zh: 從露台可見一大片人群，慢慢走向車站出口。

takeaways.en: She described a sea of people at the festival, while the report used the organisers’ checked attendance figures.
takeaways.zh: 她描述節慶有一大片人群，報告則用主辦人核過入場數字。

brief.meaningEn: Begin to appear or become part of a situation gradually, often without being noticed at first.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸開始出現或進入某情況，起初往往不易察覺。
brief.grammar: doubt/errors/a habit creeps or crept in; creeping in. Into introduces an explicit affected situation: stress can creep into everyday life. Both emotional states and outside influences may gradually enter a situation; the destination does not create a separate sense.
brief.register: Common figurative phrasal verb; literal slow movement is another use. The phrase need not suggest deliberate wrongdoing or a sudden dramatic event.
brief.boundaryZh: 逐漸出現不表示有人故意造成，也不必已全面掌控或不能處理；需看具體早期線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以及早注意並調整，不等到問題很大才承認，也不因有疑慮便判一定失敗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述漸起的變化及可見跡象，保留原因與程度未知。

listening.en: Doubt crept in after several unanswered messages about the rehearsal: I began wondering whether the plan was still going ahead, though a missing reply was not proof that anyone wanted to cancel it.
listening.zh: 幾次排練訊息沒回覆後，疑慮漸起；我開始想計劃是否仍照辦，但沒回覆不證明有人想取消。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼逐漸改變，沒有確定甚麼？

options.en: Unanswered messages led to growing uncertainty, without establishing that the rehearsal was cancelled.
options.zh: 沒回訊息令疑慮漸增，卻未確立排練取消。

options.en: A cancellation notice arrived first and confirmed that the room would not be used.
options.zh: 先收到取消通知，確認房間不用。

options.en: The speaker remained entirely certain about every arrangement throughout.
options.zh: 說話者一直完全確定每項安排。

options.en: Everyone had replied with the same confirmed time before any doubt appeared.
options.zh: 疑慮出現前，每人已回同一確定時間。

listening.explanationZh: crept in指疑慮逐漸起，不是已收到取消或安排全確認。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想再確認排練安排？
reply.promptEn: Why would you like to check the rehearsal arrangements again?

options.en: Doubt has crept in because several messages have gone unanswered.
options.zh: 幾次訊息沒回，疑慮已不知不覺出現。

options.en: I am becoming less sure whether the plan is still going ahead.
options.zh: 我開始不太確定計劃是否仍照辦。

options.en: The lack of replies leaves a question that a direct check could answer.
options.zh: 沒回覆留下問題，直接確認或可解答。

options.en: I do not want to turn growing uncertainty into an assumption that the rehearsal is cancelled.
options.zh: 我不想把漸增疑慮變成排練已取消的假定。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答未回覆與不確定的關係，未當取消已證。

scene.promptZh: 你們每周整理資料，一開始用同一標籤，後來幾位成員悄悄用不同拼法，近期才發現檢索會漏；還未知道誰最先改。哪句準確？

options.en: Inconsistent spellings have crept in over time, but we have not traced how the differences began.
options.zh: 拼法不一致逐漸出現，但未追出差異怎開始。

options.en: The whole system was deliberately replaced in one announced change.
options.zh: 整套系統在一次已公布改動中被刻意替換。

options.en: Every label still uses the original spelling, so no variation has appeared.
options.zh: 每個標籤仍用原拼法，沒有變體。

scene.explanationZh: 逐步變出差異符合，未有一次全面改或故意由誰開始的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個描述最不像 creep in 的逐漸、不易察覺特點？

options.en: A habit develops through small repeated changes before someone notices it.
options.zh: 習慣經細小重複改動形成，之後才被留意。

options.en: A planned replacement happens all at once at an announced time.
options.zh: 計劃好的替換在已公布時間一次發生。

options.en: Uncertainty starts to affect someone’s thinking without a single decisive announcement.
options.zh: 沒有單一決定性宣布，不確定卻開始影響思考。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次已公布替換缺這裏逐漸不易察覺特點。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見你有疑慮，便想把排練刪出日程；你只是未收回覆，仍可問清。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Doubt has crept in, but let us ask directly before treating the rehearsal as cancelled.
options.zh: 疑慮漸起，但先直接問清，不把排練當取消。

options.en: Remove the rehearsal from everyone’s calendar before asking anyone about the unanswered messages.
options.zh: 未問任何人沒回訊息的原因，先刪大家日程中的排練。

options.en: Send the same message repeatedly to the same silent chat instead of checking who can confirm the booking.
options.zh: 不找可確認訂房的人，只向同一無回覆群組重發同樣訊息。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把不確定轉成可查問題，不未問便取消或無改方法重發。

speaking.en: Small errors can creep in when we copy the list repeatedly, so let us compare the versions before assigning blame.
speaking.zh: 清單反覆複製時，小錯可不知不覺出現，所以歸責前先比版本。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說逐漸變化及可查的下一步。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你改小說日記，角色原本喜歡晚間畫畫，後來每天先回一則工作訊息，慢慢變成整晚等通知，近日才察覺沒再畫。你想寫這習慣如何漸入生活，再讓她試一晚先關通知畫十分鐘，不宣告工作全有害。用一至兩句英文寫。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用日常細小累積說習慣漸入，接一晚有限嘗試，不把逐漸變化寫成一次決定或全盤否定工作。

examples.en: The habit of waiting for work messages had crept in until drawing disappeared from her evenings. She decided to silence the notifications for ten minutes and begin one sketch before checking again.
examples.zh: 等工作訊息的習慣漸入，直到晚間畫畫消失；她決定關通知十分鐘，先開始一張速寫，再查訊息。

examples.en: Work checking crept in one small message at a time, not through a single decision to give up art. That evening she set aside ten quiet minutes to draw before returning to the phone.
examples.zh: 查工作訊息從一則一則漸入，不是一次決定放棄藝術；那晚她先留十分鐘安靜畫畫，再回手機。

takeaways.zh: 討論中不同假定不知不覺出現，主席請大家說明各自理解。

brief.meaningEn: Have one’s available capacity or resources used to the fullest extent, with little or no room for more demands.
brief.meaningZh: 可用能力或資源已盡用，幾乎沒有餘力接更多要求。
brief.grammar: a team/resources are stretched to the limit; a demand can stretch capacity to the limit, with the resource object between verb and complement. This lesson’s assessed models use the passive capacity frame.
brief.register: Established capacity metaphor. It differs from a manageable challenge that stretches learning; the limit concerns available room for additional demands.
brief.boundaryZh: 已到極限不等於已失敗或每人能力差，也不能只靠人少便推極限；需有工作量及資源根據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 能完成現有工作不代表仍可無限加任務；可核優先次序、範圍及可用支援。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述接近滿載的具體根據，提出有界限的安排。

listening.en: The caption team was stretched to the limit: every editor already had a full set of pages, so adding the new interviews would mean delaying something else unless another editor could join.

listening.promptZh: 現有負荷與加工作的關係是甚麼？

options.en: Capacity was already full, so more interviews required extra help or a changed timetable.
options.zh: 能力已滿，加訪談需額外幫手或改時間表。

options.en: The editors had no pages assigned and were waiting for their first task.

options.en: The new interviews had already been finished without changing any assignments.

options.en: The team is stretched to the limit, with every editor already assigned a full set of pages.
options.zh: 每位編輯已有整批頁，小組負荷已到極限。

options.en: We would need another editor or a delay to fit the interviews into the current workload.
options.zh: 要把訪談加進現有工作量，需多一編輯或延期。

options.en: Accepting them now would displace work we have already promised to finish.

options.en: There is no spare editing time in the present assignments.
options.zh: 現有分工沒有多餘編輯時間。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由 stretched to the limit 推出？

options.en: Available resources have little room for extra demands.

options.en: Give each editor the interviews now and discuss delays only after the original deadline passes.
options.zh: 現在把訪談交每位編輯，原限期過後才談延期。

options.en: The added interviews sound quick, so we can accept them without checking their length or moving any existing work.
options.zh: 新增訪談聽來快，所以可不查長度、也不移原工作就接。

dialogue.explanationZh: 原有工作能交不代有餘量，加訪談需先核實際工夫及支援，不等逾期或只憑聽來快便接。

speaking.en: Our small team is stretched to the limit this week, so an extra task would need a change to the agreed schedule.
speaking.zh: 小組本周負荷已到極限，加任務需改議定時間表。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說容量限制及新增要求的條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替社區故事晚會編主持稿，當晚節目時間已全部分給獲邀故事，臨時又有新分享者。你想寫給伙伴說時段已滿，提議先問對方可否下次參加，或徵求現有講者自願縮短，不未問便刪人的時間。用一至兩句英文提出。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以已分完時間說滿載，給新分享者實際替代或先問自願調整，不未問便取走既定講者時間。

examples.en: The programme is stretched to the limit, with every minute already promised to the invited storytellers. Could we offer the new speaker a place next time or ask whether anyone is willing to shorten their turn?
examples.zh: 節目時間已到極限，每分鐘都已答應邀請講者；可否邀新人下次來，或問有沒有人願縮短自己的時段？

examples.en: Our schedule is stretched to the limit, so I would not insert another story by quietly cutting someone else’s time. Let us ask about a later session before changing the agreed turns.
examples.zh: 時間表已到極限，我不會偷偷刪別人時間來插新故事；改議定輪次前，先問之後場次吧。

takeaways.en: The translation team was stretched to the limit before the launch, so we reduced the optional material.
takeaways.zh: 推出前翻譯組負荷已到極限，所以我們減少非必要資料。

takeaways.en: When the shared resources are stretched to the limit, we need to agree what takes priority before accepting more work.
takeaways.zh: 共用資源負荷到極限時，接更多工作前需議優先次序。

target.pattern: \bkeep(?:s|ing)? pace with demand\b|\bkept pace with demand\b

brief.meaningEn: Maintain or increase provision sufficiently to match the level or growth of need.
brief.meaningZh: 維持或增加供應，使其足以配合需求程度或增長。
brief.grammar: a service/team can or cannot keep pace with demand; kept/keeping. Compare what is needed with what can be provided, not speed alone.
brief.register: Conventional pace-as-matching-rate metaphor. Demand can concern visits, requests or materials; more activity does not prove needs are being met.
brief.boundaryZh: 變快或做更多不表示足夠，要比較需求；跟得上也不保證每人即時獲服務或品質已核。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需同看供需，不能只用完成量上升判已追上。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述需求與供應的相對變化，提出可核的調整。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The clinic could not keep pace with demand.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 40, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The costume team repaired more each week but could not keep pace with demand after two productions joined. New requests outpaced finished repairs, so the coordinator asked directors to prioritise essential changes.
listening.zh: 服裝組每周修更多件，但多兩個製作加入後仍跟不上需求；請求比完成修補來得快，統籌請導演先排必要改動。
listening.promptZh: 為甚麼修更多仍不夠？

options.en: Requests were growing faster than completed repairs, despite increased output.
options.zh: 請求比完成修補增得更快，即使產量已升。

options.en: The team stopped all repairs when the extra productions joined.
options.zh: 額外製作加入時，小組停全部修補。

options.en: Every request had already been completed before the directors discussed priorities.
options.zh: 導演談優先次序前，每項請求已完成。

options.en: The coordinator wanted directors to order new costumes instead of comparing repair needs.
options.zh: 統籌要導演訂新服裝，不比較修補需求。

listening.explanationZh: 要比請求與完成，不只看修多；優先必要改動是所述回應。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼每周修更多後，仍要排優先次序？
reply.promptEn: Why are priorities still needed after increasing weekly repairs?

options.en: We cannot keep pace with demand because new requests are arriving faster than repairs are finished.
options.zh: 新請求比修好來得快，所以我們仍跟不上需求。

options.en: The extra productions increased the workload beyond the rise in completed repairs.
options.zh: 額外製作增加的工作量，超過修補完成量的增長。

options.en: More output is not enough when the incoming requests are growing even faster.
options.zh: 若新請求增得更快，產量增加仍不夠。

options.en: We need to decide which changes matter first while the repair queue is growing.
options.zh: 修補隊伍漸長時，我們需決定先改甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用供需差或漸長輪候答排優先的原因。

scene.promptZh: 圖書交換站加快處理，最近每周可配對二十個請求；新請求穩定每周十五個，舊輪候也在減。你想只就處理量說現況，不推每人即時拿書。哪句準確？

options.en: At this rate, the exchange is keeping pace with demand and reducing the backlog, though some people still wait.
options.zh: 按此速度，交換站跟得上需求，也減積壓，但仍有人需等。

options.en: The number processed is rising, so every reader must receive a book immediately.
options.zh: 處理量上升，所以每位讀者必即時拿書。

options.en: The remaining backlog shows that new requests still arrive faster than the exchange can process them.
options.zh: 仍有積壓顯新請求仍比處理速度快。

scene.explanationZh: 二十配對比十五新請求多，舊隊亦在減；仍有舊積壓不證新需求已超容量，也不等於每人即時拿書。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個證據最不足以單獨證明 keep pace with demand？

options.en: Completed work increases, but the rate of incoming requests has not been checked.
options.zh: 完成量增加，但未查新請求的速度。

options.en: Provision matches new requests over the period, with existing waiting work stable or falling.
options.zh: 期間供應配合新請求，舊輪候持平或減少。

options.en: The comparison considers both the needed volume and available provision.
options.zh: 比較同時考慮需求量及可用供應。

contrast.explanationZh: 只知完成量上升未有需求比較，不能單憑此判已跟上。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想用「修多三件」宣布已跟上，但新製作加入後請求增加多少還未比較。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Compare incoming requests with finished repairs before claiming we can keep pace with demand.
options.zh: 先比新請求與修好數，再稱跟得上需求。

options.en: Use the higher repair total alone and leave the new productions out of the comparison.
options.zh: 只用較高修補總數，不把新製作放進比較。

options.en: Ask for every optional change first while postponing the discussion of essential repairs.
options.zh: 延後談必要修補，先要每項非必要改動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需要供需同看，並非單看多做或先加非必要需求。

speaking.en: The service is doing more, but we need to compare new requests before saying it can keep pace with demand.
speaking.zh: 服務做得更多，但說跟得上需求前，需比較新請求。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用供需比較而非單看速度。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與朋友主持短篇互評，每人每周只能仔細讀兩篇，邀稿後來了十二篇，但兩位主持合共只能讀四篇。你想寫公開回覆，說這輪未能跟上，提分批並先問作者願否等下輪，不假裝加快看便可保持仔細回饋。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 比較十二請求與每周四篇仔細閱讀，說分批及讓作者選等，不以空泛加快保證全部即時且仔細。

examples.en: Our careful feedback cannot keep pace with demand this round: twelve stories have arrived, and we can read four properly each week. Could we arrange batches and ask which writers are willing to wait for the next round?
examples.zh: 本輪仔細回饋跟不上需求：來了十二篇，我們每周可仔細讀四篇；可否分批，問哪些作者願等下輪？

examples.en: We cannot keep pace with demand by promising immediate comments on every story. Let us offer a clear place in a later batch rather than rush the reading without the writer’s agreement.
examples.zh: 承諾每篇即時評語，不能讓我們跟上需求；與其未得作者同意便趕讀，不如清楚提供較後批次名額。

takeaways.en: The lending desk kept pace with demand after the team added a second collection session each week.
takeaways.zh: 團隊每周多加一段取件時段後，借物櫃枱跟上了需求。

takeaways.en: We were processing more forms but still could not keep pace with demand, so we checked where the queue was growing.
takeaways.zh: 雖處理更多表格，我們仍跟不上需求，所以查隊伍在哪漸長。

titleEn: the whole city breathes more easily
titleZh: 整座城市彷彿鬆了口氣

target.pattern: \bthe whole city breathes more easily\b|\bthe whole city breathed more easily\b

brief.meaningEn: Personify a city as experiencing relief when pressures on urban life are eased.
brief.meaningZh: 把城市擬人化，形容城市生活壓力緩和後彷彿鬆了口氣。
brief.grammar: the whole city breathes/breathed more easily after a change; the city stands for urban life and the people affected, not one literal breathing body.
brief.register: Creative city personification. Whole city is an expansive rhetorical description; factual reporting still needs to specify who benefits and what changed.
brief.boundaryZh: 修辭可表廣泛緩解，不能當每位居民都受惠或實際呼吸已量度改善；要有具體日常變化支持。
brief.misconceptionZh: 交通或流程改善可減部分壓力，仍可有未改善地方；不要把形象描寫當全城調查。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋城市擬人意象及所指改善，保留範圍。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: the whole city breathes more easily
sources.sentence: With better transport, the whole city breathes more easily.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 40, table 1, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: After the temporary bridge reopened, the whole city breathed more easily, the columnist wrote: the long detours eased, though her examples came from bus users and she had not surveyed every district.
listening.zh: 臨時橋重開後，專欄作者寫整座城市彷彿鬆口氣：長繞路減少，但例子來自巴士乘客，未查每區。
listening.promptZh: 這句擬人化描寫有甚麼根據及限制？

options.en: Reduced detours support an image of relief, but the examples do not establish every district’s experience.
options.zh: 繞路減少支持舒緩意象，但例子未確立每區經驗。

options.en: A citywide survey confirmed identical benefits for every resident.
options.zh: 全城調查確認每位居民所得好處相同。

options.en: The bridge remained closed and the detours became longer in the reported examples.
options.zh: 在報道例子中，橋仍關閉，繞路變更長。

options.en: The column reported measurements of residents’ breathing rather than travel changes.
options.zh: 專欄報告居民呼吸量度，而非行程改動。

listening.explanationZh: 巴士例子支持繞路緩解，不是全城調查或生理量度。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼作者用「城市鬆口氣」形容橋重開？
reply.promptEn: Why did the columnist describe the city as relieved after the bridge reopened?

options.en: The whole city breathed more easily in her image because the long detours had eased.
options.zh: 她的意象中，長繞路減少，整座城市彷彿鬆口氣。

options.en: The reopened route relieved a daily travel pressure in the examples she described.
options.zh: 在她所述例子中，重開路線減了日常交通壓力。

options.en: She was conveying relief through a city image, based on bus users’ shorter detours.
options.zh: 她據巴士乘客繞路縮短，用城市意象表緩解。

options.en: The change gave her a way to describe urban life feeling less burdened.
options.zh: 改動讓她可形容城市生活較少負擔。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以繞路減少解釋修辭，不把城市當一個身體或把例子當全面調查。

scene.promptZh: 你讀一篇虛構城市散文，修好公共時鐘後人們不用再反覆等錯班次；作者寫全城鬆口氣，但只跟三位通勤者談過。哪句準確？

options.en: The phrase the whole city breathes more easily conveys relief, but three accounts do not prove that every resident benefits equally.
options.zh: 整座城市彷彿鬆口氣表緩解，但三人敘述不證每位居民同等受惠。

options.en: The three accounts amount to a complete survey of the city’s different districts.
options.zh: 三人敘述等於已完整調查城市各區。

options.en: The image says the clock repair has no connection with anyone’s everyday arrangements.
options.zh: 意象說修時鐘與任何人日常安排都無關。

scene.explanationZh: 可以讀出緩解意象，也保留訪談範圍，不是全查或沒有日常關連。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 the whole city breathes more easily 的修辭直接推出？

options.en: The writer presents urban life as relieved of some pressure.
options.zh: 作者把城市生活寫成部分壓力獲緩解。

options.en: A measured improvement has been established for every resident’s physical breathing.
options.zh: 已確立每位居民實際呼吸的量度改善。

options.en: The following examples can explain what pressure the writer means.
options.zh: 後面例子可解釋作者所指壓力。

contrast.explanationZh: 城市擬人不提供每人生理量度證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把作者的巴士例子改成「全城每區居民均獲證實受惠」，因她用了whole city。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the image of relief, but identify the bus users in the evidence instead of claiming a survey of every district.
options.zh: 保留舒緩意象，但證據只說巴士乘客，不稱已查每區。

options.en: Treat the expressive phrase as the completed district survey without checking how the examples were collected.
options.zh: 不查例子怎收，直接把修辭當已完成各區調查。

options.en: Remove all mention of shorter detours because not every district was interviewed.
options.zh: 未訪問每區，所以刪掉全部繞路縮短的資料。

dialogue.explanationZh: 局部例子有用但不能擴成全查，也不用因範圍有限便抹去。

speaking.en: The whole city breathed more easily in the writer’s description, though the examples showed relief for particular routes rather than everyone.
speaking.zh: 作者描寫整座城市彷彿鬆口氣，但例子顯示特定路線受惠，不是每人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分擬人描寫與事實範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替校園劇寫結尾旁白。虛構城市收到警報系統已修好的消息，街上幾人放下肩膀，商店重新開門，但遠處角色仍未收到通知。你想用城市鬆口氣的意象，再切到尚在等消息的角色，保留不同處境。用一至兩句英文寫旁白。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以舞台可見放鬆動作承載城市意象，再轉未收到消息的人，不把修辭當每人已知及全無疑慮。

examples.en: The whole city breathed more easily as doors opened and shoulders dropped along the street. Yet across the river, one family was still waiting for the message to reach them.
examples.zh: 街上門重開、人們放鬆肩膀時，整座城市彷彿鬆口氣；但河對岸一個家庭仍等消息傳來。

examples.en: In the square, it seemed that the whole city breathed more easily after the repair was announced. Across the river, Mara still sat beside the silent radio, waiting for news she had not yet heard.
examples.zh: 修好消息公布後，廣場彷彿整座城市都鬆口氣；河對岸，Mara仍坐無聲收音機旁，等還未聽到的消息。

takeaways.en: The whole city breathes more easily in the poem when the blocked routes reopen and the evening journeys become simpler.
takeaways.zh: 詩中阻路重開、晚間行程變簡，整座城市彷彿鬆了口氣。

takeaways.en: She wrote that the whole city breathed more easily, then described the commuters whose daily waits had shortened.
takeaways.zh: 她寫整座城市彷彿鬆口氣，再描述每日等候縮短的通勤者。

titleZh: 樓宇密集、缺少綠意的城市

brief.meaningEn: An urban area dominated by buildings and hard surfaces, often experienced as lacking greenery or a welcoming human scale.
brief.meaningZh: 樓宇及硬質地面占主導、常令人覺得缺綠意或欠親切尺度的城市地帶。
brief.grammar: an area feels like/is described as a concrete jungle; a conventional urban metaphor, not a measured planning category.
brief.register: Often critical or subjective description. A resident can dislike the physical setting while valuing neighbours, jobs or activities there.
brief.boundaryZh: 意象不證實無一株植物、所有居民不喜歡或沒有社群；需說具體外觀與誰的感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 批評建成環境與肯定居民生活可並存，不把地方標籤變居民評價。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以可見城市特徵支持描寫，保留人與地方的多面性。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The district felt like a concrete jungle before the park opened.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 40, table 1, row 8; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: To me, the new district felt like a concrete jungle, with tall blocks and few places to sit under trees; I still valued the neighbours who welcomed us and the busy library at the corner.
listening.zh: 對我而言，新區像水泥森林，高樓多，很少可坐樹下的地方；但我仍重視歡迎我們的鄰居及街角活躍圖書館。
listening.promptZh: 批評甚麼，仍重視甚麼？

options.en: The speaker disliked aspects of the built setting but valued neighbours and the library.
options.zh: 說話者不喜部分建成環境，仍重視鄰居及圖書館。

options.en: The speaker said no neighbour had welcomed them and no activities existed.
options.zh: 說話者說沒有鄰居歡迎，也沒有活動。

options.en: The account described a wooded village with very few buildings.
options.zh: 敘述描寫樹木茂密、樓宇極少的村落。

options.en: A resident survey had established that every household wanted to leave.
options.zh: 居民調查已確立每戶都想離開。

listening.explanationZh: 樓多少樹下座位是外觀感受，鄰居及圖書館仍有價值，未查全戶。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把新區形容為水泥森林？
reply.promptEn: Why do you describe the new district as a concrete jungle?

options.en: It feels like a concrete jungle to me because tall blocks dominate and shaded places are scarce.
options.zh: 高樓占主導、陰涼地方少，對我像水泥森林。

options.en: There are few places where I can sit under a tree among the tall buildings.
options.zh: 高樓間很少可坐樹下的地方。

options.en: The hard-built surroundings give me that impression, even though I value the community.
options.zh: 硬質建成環境給我那印象，雖然我重視社群。

options.en: The dominating towers and scarce shaded seating shape my description of the setting, not a judgement about the neighbours.
options.zh: 高樓主導及陰涼座位少，形成我對環境的描述，不是評鄰居。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以建成環境回應比喻，沒有把居民貶低。

scene.promptZh: 小說人物回到樓宇密集的街區，覺得廣場太硬太空，卻記得每晚跟街坊下棋；你想保留她的複雜感受。哪句貼切？

options.en: The area felt like a concrete jungle to her, yet it also held the neighbours and games she missed.
options.zh: 對她像水泥森林，但也有她掛念的街坊及棋局。

options.en: Her description is a complaint about the neighbours’ treatment of her, rather than the square.
options.zh: 她的描寫是在抱怨鄰居怎對她，不是廣場環境。

options.en: The chess memories make her account wholly positive about the square’s hard open space.
options.zh: 棋局回憶讓她對廣場硬質空間的敘述全然正面。

scene.explanationZh: 建成環境負面感受與人際正面記憶並存；不是抱怨鄰居，也不是對廣場全正面。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a concrete jungle 的形容推出？

options.en: Buildings and hard surfaces dominate the speaker’s impression.
options.zh: 樓宇及硬地占說話者印象主導。

options.en: The people living there have no community life or valued relationships.
options.zh: 住在那裏的人沒有社群生活或重視的關係。

options.en: The speaker can explain a lack of greenery in the setting.
options.zh: 說話者可解釋環境缺綠意的感受。

contrast.explanationZh: 環境比喻不判居民全無關係。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把你批評少樹下座位改成「那裏的人都冷漠」，但鄰居明明歡迎你。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the comment about the built setting and the welcome from neighbours; one does not cancel the other.
options.zh: 保留建成環境的評論及鄰居歡迎，兩者不互相取消。

options.en: Use the building description to replace what the neighbours actually did.
options.zh: 用建築描寫取代鄰居實際做過的事。

options.en: Focus the account only on the library interior and leave the concern about outdoor shade unmentioned.
options.zh: 敘述只聚焦圖書館內部，不提對戶外樹蔭的顧慮。

dialogue.explanationZh: 物理環境及居民行動分層寫，不互相代證或抹除。

speaking.en: The area felt like a concrete jungle to me, but that did not describe the warmth of the people who lived there.
speaking.zh: 該區對我像水泥森林，但這不描述住在那裏的人的熱情。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分地方外觀與居民經驗。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為一張學生城市照片配文字，照片滿是高樓及硬地，畫面外卻有小公園和居民聚餐；你想把「水泥森林」限定這個鏡頭的印象，邀觀眾看第二張生活照片，不讓單一畫面定義全區。用一至兩句英文寫圖說。
writing.selfCheckZh: 限定鏡頭印象，指出第二張補充生活，不把照片沒拍到當全區不存在，也不以環境標籤評居民。

examples.en: In this frame, the towers and hard surfaces make the area look like a concrete jungle. The next photograph shows the small park and shared meal that this view leaves out.
examples.zh: 這鏡頭中，高樓硬地讓該區像水泥森林；下張照片展示這角度沒拍到的小公園及聚餐。

examples.en: This view suggests a concrete jungle, but it is only one part of the district’s life. Look at the second image for the neighbours gathering beyond the edge of this frame.
examples.zh: 這角度給水泥森林印象，但只是該區生活一部分；可看第二張，見鏡頭邊緣外鄰居聚會。

takeaways.zh: 敘述者稱該區水泥森林，後來想起店後藏着的小花園。

takeaways.en: It looked like a concrete jungle from the train, though that brief view could not show the neighbourhood’s whole life.
takeaways.zh: 從火車看像水泥森林，但那短角度不能展示街區全部生活。

titleZh: 在重重限制中勉強生活

brief.meaningEn: Live with very little room, freedom or capacity because of restrictive conditions, using an image of squeezing through a narrow space.
brief.meaningZh: 借擠過狹窄空間的意象，形容生活受限制，空間、自由或餘力很少。
brief.grammar: people squeeze through life; squeezed/squeezing. This is a contextual whole-life image, not an established separate dictionary idiom or a literal description of body size.
brief.register: Creative constraint metaphor. Explain the actual restrictions and whose account it represents; do not use it as a judgement of a group’s character or worth.
brief.boundaryZh: 受限不等於沒有主動性或所有方面都差，也不能未聽本人便替他定義一生；需具體生活根據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可指出安排造成的限制，保留人正在做的選擇，不把困難全歸個人。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋狹窄意象所指限制，描述具體可調部分而不概括他人整個人生。

sources.sentence: No family should have to squeeze through life in unsafe housing.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 40, table 1, row 9; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The narrator felt she was squeezing through life between a crowded flat and changing shifts; she still treasured the weekly choir, but kept having to ask for a different practice time when the rota changed.
listening.zh: 敘述者覺得在擠迫住處及變動班次之間勉強生活；她仍珍惜每周合唱，卻常因班表改而需問另一練習時間。
listening.promptZh: 意象所指限制及仍有價值的是甚麼？

options.en: Limited space and changing hours constrained her routine, while the choir still mattered to her.
options.zh: 空間有限和工時變動限制日常，合唱仍對她重要。

options.en: The narrator had stopped valuing music and chosen never to sing again.
options.zh: 敘述者已不重視音樂，選永不再唱。

options.en: The flat and work rota were both spacious and predictable in her account.
options.zh: 按她敘述，住處寬敞，班表也可預期。

options.en: The phrase reported her physical measurements rather than her living arrangements.
options.zh: 詞組報她身體尺寸，不是生活安排。

listening.explanationZh: 住處班表限制是根據，合唱價值仍在；不是尺寸或已棄音樂。

reply.promptZh: 她為甚麼用勉強擠過生活這個意象？
reply.promptEn: Why does she use the image of squeezing through life?

options.en: She feels she is squeezing through life because limited space and changing hours leave little flexibility.
options.zh: 空間有限且工時常改，少彈性，讓她覺得勉強擠過生活。

options.en: Her routine has to fit around both a crowded home and an unpredictable rota.
options.zh: 她的日常要配合擠迫住處及不易預期班表。

options.en: The changing shifts make it difficult to protect the choir time she values.
options.zh: 班次變動令她難保珍惜的合唱時間。

options.en: The image captures the narrow room for choice in the arrangements she describes.
options.zh: 意象表她所述安排中，選擇餘地很窄。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以實際限制答意象，不把人物說成沒有價值或完全不選擇。

scene.promptZh: 你讀一篇訪問，受訪者說每天需在很窄的工作時段內照顧家庭、通勤及兼讀，但仍主動改課表以保留學習。你想尊重她的限制及行動。哪句準確？

options.en: Her account of squeezing through life describes restrictive arrangements, not an absence of effort or choice.
options.zh: 她勉強擠過生活的敘述指安排受限，不是沒有努力或選擇。

options.en: The image shows that she has made no attempt to adjust her study arrangements.
options.zh: 意象顯示她沒有嘗試調整學習安排。

options.en: Her decision to alter the timetable proves that the travel and care constraints have disappeared.
options.zh: 她決定改課表，證明通勤及照顧限制已消失。

scene.explanationZh: 主動調課與仍受限並存，不抹努力或把改表當全解。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 squeeze through life 的生活意象推出？

options.en: The described conditions leave a person little room to manoeuvre.
options.zh: 所述條件令某人少有調整餘地。

options.en: The person has no agency and nothing valuable in life.
options.zh: 那人沒有自主性，生活也沒有有價值事物。

options.en: A writer should identify the practical restrictions behind the image.
options.zh: 作者應指出意象背後的實際限制。

contrast.explanationZh: 生活受限不等於否定人的行動及價值。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把敘述者改練習時間寫成她不在乎合唱，你知道她常問正是想保留它。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Explain how the rota restricts her, while showing that asking for another time is an effort to keep the choir in her life.
options.zh: 說明班表怎限制她，也寫出問另一時間是努力保留合唱。

options.en: Count each request to change time as a separate decision to leave the choir.
options.zh: 把每次請求改時間，都算成一次離開合唱團的決定。

options.en: Leave the shift changes out and describe only whether she attended on the original day.
options.zh: 刪班次改動，只寫她有沒在原日出席。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把限制及想保留的行動連起，不把求改時間當退團或刪去情境。

speaking.en: She described squeezing through life under the changing arrangements, while still making room for the people and interests she valued.
speaking.zh: 她說在變動安排下勉強擠過生活，卻仍為珍惜的人與興趣留位置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分生活限制與人的行動價值。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你受訪時用這意象形容目前擠迫住處及輪班；記者卻擬標題「她一生沒有選擇」，刪掉你主動兼讀及喜愛合唱的話。你想回覆要求保原話的情境、先讓你看引文，不把困難變成你整個身份。用一至兩句英文寫給記者。

examples.en: When I said I was squeezing through life, I meant my present housing and shifts, not that I had no choices or interests. Please keep my study and choir in the context and let me check the quotation before it is published.
examples.zh: 我說勉強擠過生活，是指目前住房及班次，不是沒選擇興趣；請保兼讀合唱的情境，刊前讓我核引文。

examples.en: Squeezing through life describes part of my current situation, not the whole of who I am. Please show me the quotation in context before publication, keeping the actions I am taking as well as the pressures rather than turning one image into my entire identity.
examples.zh: 勉強擠過生活描述我現況一部分，不是整個我；刊前請讓我看有情境的引文，保我正做的行動及壓力，不把一意象變整個身份。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫受訪者對引文情境及個人身份的回覆，保真實限制與行動，要求刊前核查。

takeaways.en: He felt he was squeezing through life around other people’s schedules and began asking which arrangements could be shared.
takeaways.zh: 他覺得按別人時間表勉強生活，開始問哪些安排可分擔。

takeaways.en: The novel’s image of squeezing through life drew attention to the cramped routine without erasing the character’s humour.
takeaways.zh: 小說勉強擠過生活的意象突顯擠迫日常，卻未抹去人物幽默。

brief.meaningEn: Become or cause a route or system to become blocked or slow because too much material or traffic is in it.
brief.meaningZh: 因過多物料或流量，令路線或系統堵塞、運作變慢，或變成這種狀態。
brief.grammar: a road is clogged up with traffic; traffic clogs up the road. A pronoun object can be separated: clog it up. Assessed examples here focus on the blocked-route/system result.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for blockage, used for drains, traffic and figurative flows of work. The source concerns a road, not a claim that roads are literally pipes.
brief.boundaryZh: 堵塞可使慢或暫不能通，不必永久停用；需看堵在哪裏，不能由一處塞推整個系統全壞。
brief.misconceptionZh: 清一處堵塞與查其他環節可分開，不必把所有人或所有流程一併停下。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述阻滯位置及原因，提出針對性的查處。
